findings.title: Protection reduction and legacy migration do not preserve the approved same-user authority boundary
findings.reproduction: Compare ECR-0004.packet.json task T03 criteria 2-5 and rollback item 5 with ADR-0018 lines 122-124 and the current v1 profile behavior in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/application_lock.rs lines 193-220. The packet requires current-provider authentication only when switching between protected modes; changing an enabled mode to none requires only confirmed intent, and a corrupt or Hello-unavailable locked state may be reset to none merely from the current interactive Windows session after confirmation/audit. ECR-0004-experience-proposal.md lines 52-69 and the HTML reference lines 81-89 expose the same unauthenticated reset. Confirmation and session presence are not proof that the same user who selected the protection authorized its removal, while accepted ADR-0018 permits corrupt-profile replacement only after successful same-user reauthentication. Separately, the packet maps an absent legacy configuration to none but never specifies the mapping for an existing valid application-lock-profile.v1.json. A persisted v1 profile with inactivityTimeoutMinutes 0 remains a user-selected password/manual-lock profile in current tested behavior, so an implementation can silently map it to none and still claim the packet's incomplete migration criterion passed. `planctl ecr validate ECR-0004` returns valid because these are substantive decision omissions rather than structural errors.
findings.requiredRemediation: Create a strict-descendant inert R02 packet revision that makes the principal and migration rules exact across the canonical proposal, packet criteria, experience proposal, HTML reference, static/generated review surfaces, and refreshed hashes. Require successful verification by the currently configured provider, or a separately specified OS-owned same-user recovery proof compatible with ADR-0018, before every protected-to-none transition and every corrupt/unavailable-provider reset; warning, confirmation, audit, or possession of the signed-in session alone must not remove protection. If no approved proof is available, remain locked and direct the user to Windows/provider recovery rather than resetting policy. Freeze legacy mapping explicitly: an absent profile becomes none, every valid persisted v1 profile becomes windows-password while preserving profile name, inactivity/restart/manual-lock semantics, and invalid/unreadable protected state stays locked until verified recovery. Add criterion-linked migration fixtures and adversarial tests for unauthenticated disable/reset, unavailable Hello, persisted v1 with zero and nonzero timeout, absent v1, and corrupt/unknown v1. If an unauthenticated reset is intentionally desired, obtain a superseding architecture/security decision that explicitly replaces ADR-0018 instead of claiming compatibility. Preserve this R01 ledger append-only and request bounded R02 review before human approval or bootstrap.

verified: The exact candidate 69d0acf2ac58c60254e955376c99f58f4deb373d is checked out on codex/w1-windows-local-runtime and directly descends from 85c3b7af4dc238ca767445a7a64f8d436282af80. Its 15-path delta contains the inert ECR-0004 proposal, packet, proposed experience/reference, static and generated review surfaces, one generic review-site renderer change, and focused renderer tests; it changes no backlog, product source, accepted ADR, canonical approved design reference, approval record, release gate, or predecessor authority.

The ECR-0004 packet SHA-256 is 3a4e355d9617923c1bed5801032e6e343a198c59180f60e534af8679b43ff2f3. The canonical proposal, v4 schema, static human review, experience proposal, and HTML reference hashes all match the packet declarations and exact current candidate bytes. Git whitespace validation passes.

`planctl ecr validate ECR-0004` passes Draft 2020-12 structure and historical authority validation. The immutable W1 base, adopted W1.A01-W1.A03 chain, uniquely introduced W1.A04 approval reservation, and exact adopted GOV-MIG-0001 file/review commit are complete, ordered, ancestral, hash-bound, and unchanged.

W1 is PAUSED at Wave scope with no lease, no W1 task in IN_PROGRESS or REVIEW, no active recovery hold, and no active amendment campaign. CAP-02.S04.T02 is DONE. The proposal remains pending and non-executable; approval, bootstrap, task claim, amendment materialization/adoption, Wave resume, gate action, merge, push, external effect, and destructive action are not granted.

The refactor denominator is reconstructed from all W1 tasks at approved base commit 594e63be501711d67d17a4aef176bb9b6a8748be using S=1, M=3, L=5 and totals 194 points. T01 is the sole refactor allocation at 5 points (2.6%). The owner-directed exception is explicitly limited to T01 and does not hide estimates, arithmetic, security criteria, evidence, or review duties.

The provider-neutral/native-supervisor direction, OS-owned Windows Hello adapter, typed fail-closed outcomes, renderer non-authority, no credential/PIN/biometric capture, explicit password recovery, atomic configuration publication, two-slice ordering, and task/slice/amendment review cadence are otherwise coherent with the Vision, current implementation, application-lock architecture, and ADR-0018's compatible-Hello allowance.

Microsoft's current UserConsentVerifier and IUserConsentVerifierInterop documentation confirms an OS-owned current-user availability check and desktop-window verification API suitable for consent before sensitive operations. The packet correctly defers exact adapter implementation to T02 and requires release-authoritative Windows-x64 verification; no external service or credential is introduced.

The proposed design-first sequence is otherwise sound: exact ECR approval reserves RO-UI-ACADEMIC-MINIMAL-1.4, B00 must materialize the canonical reference and approval record in a separate independently reviewed commit, and renderer implementation cannot begin before that reference commit. The proposal clearly separates Application Settings from Project Settings and covers scope, provider states, no-silent-fallback, redaction, keyboard/focus/announcement, responsive, theme, reduced-motion, and WCAG AA obligations.

The generated review-site loader recomputes governed-experience hashes through repository-safe paths and renders reservation, migration, dynamic slice/task inventory, itemized refactor policy, and proposed experience fields from packet data. `plan_review_check.py` passes for 19 capabilities, 111 slices, 337 tasks, and 488 HTML pages; the focused site suite passes 15 tests in 18.847 seconds, including hash-tamper denial and dynamic ECR-0004 rendering.

Focused controls pass: tests.foundation.test_planctl_amendments passes 8 tests in 109.931 seconds; canonical backlog validation passes for 20 capabilities, 117 slices, 359 tasks, and 12 release gates; Python quality passes for 168 governed files. The review-site generator has no `--check` option, so deterministic site integrity was established through the canonical validator and focused generation/validation tests rather than by mutating generated files.

Rollback is bounded before approval and preserves adverse evidence after bootstrap/task/slice review, but rollback cannot cure the open same-user reset and legacy-migration authority ambiguity. Human approval is not legally available while ECR-0004-R01-F01 remains open.
